big: Rohan's fund went from ₹1 lakh to ₹1.4 lakh. He feels ₹40,000 richer. The taxman does not see it that way. Until he sells, nothing has been earned in the eyes of the tax law.

lines: My portfolio is up a lot this year. Do I owe tax on that?
Not yet. Tax comes only when you sell and lock the profit in. Until then it is a gain on paper, and prices can move again.

h: A capital gain, step by step
intro: Made-up numbers, to show the sums.
rows: No gain realised, no tax yet
note: Tax rates change with each Budget, so this course works with made-up rates. Always check the current rate before you act.

title: Capital gains basics
stops: Only a gain you have realised by selling is taxed
A rise in portfolio value is taxed every year
How long you held an asset can change the tax rate
A loss is the same thing as a gain
caps: Tax applies when you sell and the gain is locked in.
A rise in value that you have not sold is only a paper gain.
Short and long holding are taxed differently, so the holding period matters.
A loss is the opposite of a gain, and it can sometimes be used to cut tax.

q: Meena's shares rose 30% but she has not sold any. What tax does she owe on this rise?
opts: Tax on the full 30% this year
Half the tax now and half later
None yet, as she has not sold
Tax only if the market falls
why: A rise she has not sold is not taxed in the year it happens.
There is no half-and-half rule for unsold holdings.
Tax applies when she sells, not while she holds.
A fall does not trigger tax. Selling does.

q: Rohan bought fund units at ₹50,000 and sold them for ₹58,000. What is his capital gain?
why: The gain is sale value less cost of acquisition: ₹58,000 less ₹50,000.
₹58,000 is the sale value, and it includes his own original money.
₹50,000 is what he paid. It is the cost, not the gain.
₹1,08,000 adds the two numbers together, which is not how a gain is found.

q: Why does the holding period matter to the tax?
opts: It can change the tax rate
It sets the broker's fee for the year
It has no link to tax at all
why: A fund's name has nothing to do with how long a person holds it.
The law treats gains from short and long holding differently, often at different rates.
Broker fees depend on trade terms and not on the tax treatment.
The period is one of the main facts used to decide the tax.

q: Meena's portfolio is up ₹2 lakh on paper. A friend says she should sell it all 'to avoid tax'. What is wrong with that?
opts: Tax on paper gains is due each December
Friends decide a person's tax rate
Selling is what creates the tax
why: Selling a gain is exactly what can bring a tax bill.
Paper gains are not taxed each December. Only realised gains are.
The tax rate comes from law and not from friends.
Tax arises on selling, so selling to avoid it is backwards.

pts: A capital gain is sale value less cost. Only a realised gain is taxed.
A rise you have not sold is a paper gain, with no tax yet.
Holding period can change the tax rate, so check current rules.
